summary.text: A 67-year-old man with a past medical history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia type II, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease and end-stage renal disease on intermittent hemodialysis presented for left atrial appendage occlusion with the Watchman device. Six months earlier he had a non-ST segment elevation myocardial infarction while taking apixaban, which was subsequently discontinued after EGD findings. Procedure-day platelet count was 85,000 cells/mcL.

Argatroban was chosen for intraoperative anticoagulation. General anesthesia was induced intravenously with fentanyl, propofol and rocuronium, the patient was intubated, and a norepinephrine infusion maintained mean arterial pressure above 65 mmHg. Baseline ACT was 136 s with a goal at or above 300 s. A reduced argatroban dose of 25 mg was given as two 12.5 mg boluses.

Five minutes after the full dose the ACT was 489 s, which was supratherapeutic, so the infusion was not initiated. About 45 minutes after the initial bolus the ACT was 262 s, prompting an infusion at 25 mcg/kg/min; about 5 minutes later the ACT was 526 s and the infusion was stopped. The procedure was then completed.

About 1 hour after the infusion was stopped, PT was 23.0 s, INR 2.0 and ACT 370 s. The patient emerged from anesthesia without complications and was admitted to the hospital to receive hemodialysis the next day. There were no documented thromboembolic or hemorrhagic complications, and hemoglobin decreased mildly by 0.7 g/dL by postoperative day 1.
